text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics is disappointed by the level of technological support it receives from the Dutch government. (p1)
- Dutch securities board STE taken to court by trader, who went bankrupt because of involvement with Nusse Brink Brokerage. (p1)
- Majority in parliament wants banks and insurers to be included in the preventive check of the merger control body that is to be established. (p1)
- Sweets maker Van Melle books 5.8 pct higher 1996 net at Dfl 51.1 million; results pressured by advertising costs. (p3)
- Shipping experts estimate the Nedlloyd and P&O container shipping group P&O Nedlloyd is heading towards co-operation with The Grand Alliance. (p3)
- Suspension of payment of TV station Sport 7 now definitive. (p4)
- Music and film company PolyGram sets up a division for production and distribution of TV programmes. (p5)
- Venture capital fund Atlas Venture reports its 1996 profit more than doubled from Dfl 42.7 million to Dfl 114.1 million. (p11)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Subsidies disturb the economic development in the long run and harm the environment - research institute of government spending. (p2)
- Brewer Heineken has evacuated a small number of its staff from the city of Kisangani, Zaire. (p2)
- Research institute TNO develops technique for proving the use of chemcial weapons against people. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- First match in the champions league quarter finals between Ajax Amsterdam and Atletico Madrid ends 1-1. (p1)
- Dutch market for alcoholic drinks has beeen flooded with bootleg liquor in the past two years. (p1)
- Employers association VNO-NCW calls for an extra nine billion guilders economy measures. (p35)
- Philips plans to restructure its own machine plants again soon. (p37)
TROUW
- Dutch rail NS's rival Lovers Rail gets permission to extend its lines. (p1)
- Medium-sized businesses are very optimistic about the economic prospects. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- ABN Amro bank upbeat about investment possibilities in Germany. (p9)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
